key_insight: This study shows that health misinformation detection in low-resource languages can be improved by combining small language models with a culturally sensitive responsible NLP framework.
clinical_relevance: For clinicians and public health teams serving Bangla-speaking communities, this approach could help identify misleading health claims and support more trustworthy patient information workflows.
method: Used a Bangla-translated health misinformation dataset
Compared multiple small language models for claim extraction
Added a Responsible NLP framework focused on cultural sensitivity, potential harm, and communication quality
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Phi-4 performed best, achieving the strongest balance of precision and recall for claim extraction in the evaluated setup.
watch_item: Performance may still be limited by translated data, low-resource language coverage, and the need to validate real-world usefulness across diverse Bangla-speaking communities.
paper_title: Evaluating Health Misinformation in Low-Resource Languages: Integrating Small Language Models with a Culturally-Sensitive Responsible NLP Framework (Bangla as a Case Study)
